page.text:
The two parts of the Fundamental Theorem of Calculus forge the crowning synthesis
of real analysis, demonstrating that differentiation and integration are mutually
inverse operations:
$$ \frac{d}{dx} \left( \int_a^x f(t) \, dt \right) = f(x) \quad \text{and} \quad \int_a^b f'(x) \, dx = f(b) - f(a). $$
Part I shows that every continuous function admits an antiderivative defined
geometrically as an area accumulator. Part II shows that any antiderivative
permits the exact analytical evaluation of a definite integral without computing
infinite limits of Riemann sums.
